extra.message: User-controlled sort column from the 'x-directory-sort' header (app/api/reports/patient-directory/route.ts:8) is interpolated directly into a SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(): ORDER BY "${column}" ASC. A value like lastName" DESC, pg_sleep(5)-- changes the query shape, enabling SQL injection. Unlike the sibling fetchSortedAppointmentQueue, no allow-list is applied.

renderReferralLetter() builds a shell command via execSync(`pandoc ${sourcePath} -o ${outputPath}`) where the format parameter (from ?format= in app/api/visit-summaries/referral-letter/route.ts:11) is embedded into outputPath with no sanitization and no allow-list. A format value such as 'md && curl attacker' yields arbitrary OS command execution as the server user.

printSpecimenLabel() executes spawn('sh', ['-c', `label-driver --preset ${labelPreset} --station ${stationId}`], { shell: true }) with attacker-controlled labelPreset/stationId from POST body (app/api/staff/label-print-station/route.ts:12-13, any authenticated user). Shell metacharacters in either value achieve OS command injection. The safe sibling printSpecimenLabelForChartingStation allow-lists presets and uses no shell.

The POST handler calls archiveHandledRecord() with no authentication or authorization check (no requireUser/requireRole), so any anonymous caller can set any document to ARCHIVED by documentId. The paired restore route correctly requires assertCanReviewDocument(). This lets unauthenticated attackers remove records from the review queue.

extra.message: handleResourceCheck() authorizes the utilization export with readResourceGrantClaims(), which only base64-decodes the JWT payload and never verifies the HMAC signature, expiry is not checked and scope is attacker-supplied (lib/network-access.ts:40-49). An attacker can forge the clinic_partner_grant cookie {partnerId, scope:'utilization-export', exp} and download the full utilization report. The sibling appointment-queue route correctly uses verifyResourceGrant().

extra.message: The billing summary trusts a base64 cookie (clinic_billing_scope) whose payload is simply {patientId, accountType} with no signature and no server-side ownership check. Any PATIENT can set the cookie (app/api/portal/billing-scope/route.ts:12-17 accepts an arbitrary patientId) to another patient's id and read that patient's name, insurance provider and insurance member id. The dependent-summary GET endpoint demonstrates the correct pattern by scoping to userId.

extra.message: findLocationDocumentsByStickySearch() interpolates the raw sticky search term into an XPath expression: //document[contains(name, '${stickySearchTerm}')]. The term originates from the unauthenticated ?q parameter (app/api/documents/board-search/route.ts:12). A term like '') or true() or (' makes the predicate match all catalog documents, and crafted input can mutate the query to enumerate data. The referral-board-search sibling escapes the term first.

importSharedReferralPacket() fetches documentSourceUrl supplied by the caller without validating host/protocol. The value comes from the x-partner-document-source header (app/api/partners/referral-packet-import/route.ts:15), enabling an authenticated staff user to make the server issue requests to arbitrary internal hosts (SSRF). The clearinghouse variant importVerifiedClearinghousePacket enforces an https + host allow-list, showing the intended control.

loadFrontDeskFormTemplate() joins category and formName directly into a file path and reads it back to the caller. Both come from an unvalidated POST body (app/api/forms/library-item/route.ts:8). formName of '../../../.env' (category '..') reads an arbitrary server file whose content is returned as the HTTP body. loadIntakePrintTemplate() reduces the name with path.basename() first, showing the intended control.

extra.message: importPatientsAction() gates only on requireUser() instead of CLINIC_ADMIN (compare import/patients API route which requires CLINIC_ADMIN), so any authenticated user - including patients - can bulk-import up to 100 fabricated patient records with arbitrary demographics, corrupting the roster.

The dispense-check endpoint requires only requireUser() and looks up any prescription by the x-prescription-ref header with no patient/ownership scoping (fetchPrescriptionForHandoffScan). Any authenticated user, including a patient, can supply another patient's prescription id and read medication, dosage, instructions and the patient's full name. The pickup-status route demonstrates the correct scope-by-owner pattern.

extra.message: submitSpecialtyReferralDispatch() sends a hardcoded Bearer credential 'rfn_9f2c7a41e8b0d3f6a5c9e2b7d4f1a8c3' to the partner network. Secrets baked into source can leak through version control and can never be rotated. The DME order path correctly reads its token from DME_NETWORK_PARTNER_TOKEN.

continueAfterConfirmation() redirects to a destination derived from the x-redirect-url header with only a startsWith('/') prefix check. A value of '//evil.com' (or '\evil.com' on Windows-parsing clients) passes the prefix check and redirects the browser off-origin. The equivalent helper for shared visit summaries validates destination.origin === request origin before redirecting.

attachHandoffExportHeaders() places the unvalidated packetLabel query parameter into the Content-Disposition response header without stripping CR/LF (used by app/api/documents/handoff-export/route.ts:29). packetLabel containing %0d%0a can inject additional response headers/body framing. The print-label route uses the sanitized variant attachSanitizedHandoffExportHeaders which strips [\r\n], showing the intended control.

extra.message: linkKey() silently falls back to the hardcoded secret 'clinic-share-link-default-secret' when CLINIC_LINK_SECRET is unset, and the visit-summary link cipher is AES-CBC with no authentication tag. If deployed without the env var, share-link tokens (which expose released visit summaries with diagnosis/instructions to anyone holding the token) can be forged or tampered with. request-integrity.ts:4 and webhook paths have analogous fallbacks.

syncApprovedRefillToPbm() embeds the PBM_API_KEY in the URL query string (?apiKey=...). Query strings are frequently logged by proxies/servers and leak through history, exposing the credential. The clearinghouse sync correctly sends the key in an Authorization header.

extra.message: exportDocumentToReferringDrop() writes the uploaded document to path.join(dropRoot(), document.category, document.originalName). document.originalName is set from the raw upload file.name (app/actions.ts:394), which a malicious client can set to contain ../ segments; when a front-desk/admin user later sends the document to the referring-office drop (actions.ts:422), the write escapes the intended category directory (arbitrary file write with partially attacker-chosen content).
